What comes up in Shellharbour

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. What follows is how this work normally runs in the area, not a reading of any one block.

Site cut on an estate block

Bringing a coastal subdivision lot to the platform level the design calls for.

How it is handled
Topsoil stripped and kept separate, the cut taken to design level, and the spoil classified once and carted on the same contract.
What does it
Midi to large excavator, truck and dog where the street allows it.

Older coastal dwelling

Established housing where the sheeting has been in the salt air for decades.

How it is handled
Condition assessed before anything is touched, removal under licence where it is asbestos, then the structure down once clearance is issued.
What does it
Licensed asbestos removalists, then an excavator with a grapple.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Shellharbour

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Coastal subdivisions and newer estate land A mix of ordinary knockdowns and site preparation ahead of construction.
  • Flatter ground than the suburbs under the escarpment Which makes the earthworks simpler and the truck access better.
  • Older coastal housing in the established parts Where weathered fibro is common and its condition decides the controls.
  • Distance from Sydney disposal facilities So the haul is a real part of the price and the classification is done properly before material moves.

Shellharbour blocks and streets are generally generous enough for a truck and dog, which matters on a site cut where the volume is real. The constraint is usually the haul rather than the block.

Shellharbour questions

What people ask before we start

Do you travel this far south?
Yes. The corridor runs from Wollongong through to Newcastle and the Illawarra is part of it. Travel is accounted for honestly in the quote rather than hidden in the rates, and if a job is too far out to be economic we will say so.
What decides where the spoil goes?
The classification, not the distance. Material is tested and classified before it moves, and it goes to a facility licensed to receive that classification.
What happens if the fill turns out to be contaminated?
It is tested and classified before it moves, then taken to a facility licensed to receive that classification. Given the industrial history around Wollongong this is a real possibility rather than a remote one, and remediation can sit on the same contract.
Does the asbestos work sit under your demolition licence?
No. Demolition licence AD214737 covers the structure. Removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists and clearance by an independent licensed assessor, because the assessor has to be independent of whoever did the removal. All of it is scheduled as a single job.
